title: Emil Kamalov
text:
I am a Postdoctoral Research Scholar at the Harriman Institute, Columbia University. Previously, I was a Postdoctoral Fellow at the Center on Democracy, Development and the Rule of Law (CDDRL), Stanford University. I hold a PhD in Political and Social Sciences from the European University Institute (EUI), Florence. My research focuses on political behavior, transnational repression, authoritarianism, migration, and violence. I am passionate about statistics, experimental, and survey methods.

Before my PhD, I worked as a junior research fellow at Ronald F. Inglehart Laboratory for Comparative Social Research and taught quantitative methods at Higher School of Economics (HSE) and European University at Saint Petersburg. I received an MA in Sociology from HSE, and a Bachelor’s degree in Economics from a university in the middle of Russia. I also happen to have a Candidate of Sciences degree in Social Philosophy.
Alongside Ivetta Sergeeva, I am a co-founder and co-lead of two multi-wave survey projects: OutRush and ViolenceMonitor. OutRush is a panel survey of Russian emigrants who left the country due to war after February 24, 2022. ViolenceMonitor focuses on intimate partner violence and conducted victimization surveys in Russia in 2021. Both projects have received wide media coverage, both in Russia and internationally, from outlets such as The New York Times, Bloomberg, Financial Times, Al Jazeera, Deutsche Welle, CNBC, Fortune, Meduza, Forbes Russia and The Moscow Times.

title: Projects
section: OutRush: Panel Survey of Russian Political Migrants
text:
OutRush: Panel Survey of Russian Political Migrants
Together with Ivetta Sergeeva, I co-founded and co-lead the OutRush project (2022–present), a panel survey focused on Russian emigrants who left Russia after February 24, 2022. To date, we have conducted five survey waves, involving more than 20,000 respondents residing in more than 100 countries. The project employs a diverse range of research methods, including both experiments and qualitative interviews. Our collected data has received extensive media coverage (70+ references), both in Russia and internationally. Media outlets that have cited our data include:
In English: The New York Times, Bloomberg, Financial Times, Al Jazeera, Deutsche Welle, CNBC, Fortune, The Moscow Times (1), The Moscow Times (2), The Japan Times
In Russian: BBC, Deutsche Welle, Voice of America, Meduza (1), Meduza (2), Meduza (3), RBC (1), RBC (2), RBC (3), Forbes Russia, Zhivoy Gvozd, Important Stories, Rasstriga.doc, Paper (1), Paper (2), Karèn Shainyan, RTVI, Novaya Gazeta, Sever Real, VC, Feminist Anti-War Resistance, Klops, Vot Tak, Glagol, Grodno 24, Komsomolskaya Pravda, Agents Media
In other languages: Jungle.World (DE), Information (DA), Corriere Del Ticino (IT), Ceske Noviny (CS), Pravda (SK)
Based on this data, we have published several peer-reviewed articles, as well as media and policy papers.

title: Projects
section: Violence Monitor: Intimate Partner Violence in Russia
text:
Violence Monitor: Intimate Partner Violence in Russia
Together with Ivetta Sergeeva, I co-founded and co-led the Violence Monitor project, a national survey of intimate partner violence in Russia (2021–2022). The project encompasses various research methods, including several survey and field experiments designed to enhance the disclosure of intimate partner violence. Our work has received media coverage from outlets such as Forbes Russia, Moscow FM, Paper (1), Paper (2), Holod, Seven Days, Burning Hut, Sysblok, and others (see more here). We have published a report on measuring violence and its prevalence rates in Russia here, and an article on measuring intimate partner violence in Sociological Methods & Research (2026).

title: Projects
section: Support for Healthcare Reform in Russia
text:
Support for Healthcare Reform in Russia
Together with Boris Sokolov, Margarita Zavadskaya, and Ivetta Sergeeva, I conducted a survey on healthcare reform in Russia, funded by a 2020 grant from the Center for Advanced Governance (Moscow). The survey included a conjoint experiment testing whether media framing can increase public support for health reform; a paper based on these results is in progress.

title: Projects
text:
Democracy in Exile (DemEx)
I am a collaborator on Democracy in Exile: A Comparative Study of Russian Migrant Communities following the Full-Scale Invasion of Ukraine (DemEx), with Marlene Laruelle, Zuzanna Brunarska, Paul Goode, and Ivetta Sergeeva. The project is funded by the National Science Foundation (2024–2026), and OutRush panel data serve as a core component.

title: Projects
section: Building a Commons in the Russian Diaspora
text:
Building a Commons in the Russian Diaspora
I was a co-investigator on Building a Commons in the Russian Diaspora (2022–2024), with Regina Smyth (Indiana University), Ivetta Sergeeva, Margarita Zavadskaya, Veronica Kostenko, Michail Turchenko, and Andrey Semenov. The project’s outputs include the policy brief In Their Own Voice: Supporting Russia’s Wartime Migrants.

title: Projects
text:
Corruption Tolerance
From November 2021 to June 2022, I served as a Research Assistant at the European University Institute in a project led by Miriam Golden, Raymond Fisman, and Matteo Ferroni. The project aimed to measure perceptions and norms of corruption among legislators and citizens in three countries: Italy, Brazil, and Pakistan. My responsibilities included conducting descriptive statistics and managing recruitment. For the recruitment process, I automated email communications using R.
